Acceleration and adiabatic damping

After the cavity the synchronous particle has $\delta_s\neq 0$. It is made the new reference:

\[p_0'=p_0(1+\delta_s),\quad 1+\delta'=\frac{1+\delta}{1+\delta_s},\quad p_x'=\frac{p_x}{1+\delta_s},\quad p_y'=\frac{p_y}{1+\delta_s},\quad \Delta t'=\Delta t-\Delta t_s.\]

Positions are unchanged. Magnets are assumed to ramp with $p_0$ (normalised strengths fixed); the RF frequency follows $h\omega_0(p_0)$.

The physical transverse momentum $P_x=p_0 p_x$ is invariant under a longitudinal field, so $p_x\propto 1/p_0$. The Courant–Snyder action in normalised variables then scales as $J\propto 1/p_0$, and betatron amplitudes damp as

\[\frac{A(n)}{A(0)}=\sqrt{\frac{p_{\mathrm{inj}}}{p_0(n)}}.\]
